annotations.text:
APPSPIRATION — KEY SCREENS
All five at 375px, in the settled house style. Georgia for player names, system-ui with tabular numerals for everything else, ground #0D1712, brand mint on the wordmark and 'Maximum Bid' only.

The persistent Maximum Bid strip is on every screen — CAP-10 requires it visible at all times, and tapping it opens the destinations sheet.

YOUR POSITIONS — where every session starts
Discord lands you here, not on the board. Grouped in the order the wake-up actually asks: what did I win, what did I lose, what am I still holding, what am I contending in, and is my Nomination Slot free.

The outbid card carries the answer to the next question before it is asked — 'you cannot re-enter, the next legal bid is $15.0M and your Maximum Bid is $14.0M' — so nobody taps into an Auction to discover it is arithmetically gone.

The empty state is at the bottom. It is a real screen: a manager who leads nothing needs pointing somewhere.

BID BOARD
Opens unfiltered — a filtered board that looks like the whole board is how people miss auctions. Filters are position and 'Mine'; sort defaults to closing order.

Five states visible: Outbid, Lottery/Contending, You lead, Awaiting bid, and an Auction you are not involved in (no chip at all — absence is the signal, and it keeps the board quiet).

No card pulses, reddens or counts down under pressure. Time is stated as a fact.

AUCTION — the individual player
Full bid history, no anonymity at any point: Team, acting Manager, amount, timestamp, and who nominated. Seven bids shown from opening bid upward.

The bid control is DISABLED with its reason stated in words, because the next legal bid ($15.0M) is above this Team's Maximum Bid ($14.0M). The limit is visible on arrival, never discovered at submission.

Footer states the rule that has no undo: every bid is permanent, none can be cancelled, edited or lowered. There is no control for it — not disabled, absent.

COMMISSIONER CONTROL CLASS
Separated from Manager controls by FORM, not colour — colour alone would fail exactly the person it protects.

1. Manager control: solid fill, full width.
2. Commissioner control: dashed outline, never filled, on its own recessed ground behind a dashed rule and a persistent 'visible only to you' label.
3. Every override opens a reason sheet first. It shows before → after for both clocks, names the consequence in words (voiding a bid ends the Auction Phase 5h 47m sooner), and requires free text with no default and no skip.
4. Paused is unmissable. An outage that looks like a quiet period is worse than one that announces itself.

New token: admin steel #6E8592 for the dashed rule and label.

TEAMS INDEX — CAP-20 / FR-39
Added 2026-08-18. The destination the IA always listed and nothing specified. It answers one question for all thirty Teams at once: who else can actually chase this player.

WHAT IT IS NOT is most of the design. No colour, no badge, no rank, no arrow, no 'above median' chip. A comparison figure is the most tempting place in the product to acquire an opinion, and SM-C1 counts bid volume as a thing never to optimise. A greyscale screenshot of this surface is not merely readable — it is identical.

DEFAULT SORT IS TEAM NAME, alphabetical, because it is the only ordering that expresses no editorial view. Opening on a cap-space sort would make this a leaderboard.

YOUR OWN ROW IS MARKED, NOT MOVED — 2px border-strong left edge and '— you'. No pinning to the top. Finding yourself in the ordering is the function of the screen.

THE MEDIAN IS THE LOWER of the two middle values. With 30 Teams the conventional median is the mean of the 15th and 16th, which lands at $250k granularity — off the $500,000 grid and unrenderable at one decimal, which is the property that makes abbreviated money safe everywhere else. PRD §10 example 28.

EVERY ROW SUMS: Cap Space − Committed = Available, at one decimal, verifiable by hand.

BULLS AT 12 OF 12 with $8.5M is §10 example 24 sitting on the index — locked out of every non-eligible Auction with money in hand. It gets no badge either; '12 of 12' says it.

IR IS SHOWN AND SITS OUTSIDE THE TWELVE — the arithmetic managers most often get wrong by hand (§10 example 23).

FRESHNESS: this surface authorises nothing, so there is no control to disable. It takes the other branch — in anything but Live the figures carry their age.

HOUSE STYLE — SETTLED
A's fonts · B's density and card style · C's deep green.

Georgia for player names, the wordmark and the two headline labels; system-ui with tabular numerals for everything else. Flat panels, 1px borders, 3px radius, 12px padding, 7px internal gaps. Ground #0D1712, surface #15211B, brand mint #6FD3A0.

THE THREE SOURCE DIRECTIONS
Kept for reference. The house style to the left is what we build from; these stay so the reasoning is legible later.

DIRECTION A — LEDGER
The private-bank statement. No cards at all: hairline rules and alignment do the work, serif player names, warm near-black.

TAKEN: the type pairing — Georgia names against a sans with tabular numerals.
LEFT: the cardless ruled board, and the warm near-black ground.

DIRECTION B — TERMINAL
Trading desk that recycles. Monospace throughout, cool near-black, boxed panels, tight rows, left-edge colour bars for state.

TAKEN: the density and the card treatment — flat bordered panels, near-square corners, tight gaps, left-edge accent bar for Lottery.
LEFT: monospace everywhere and the uppercase body copy, which was fatiguing to read and fought the banking voice.

DIRECTION C — SUSTAINABLE
The literal read of the brief: soft elevated cards, 14px radii, pill chips, deep green-black ground.

TAKEN: the deep green-black ground and the mint brand colour — the half that carries the Aspiration pun.
LEFT: the 14px radii, pill chips and card shadows, which cost vertical room the board cannot spare.

RULES THIS ARTBOARD ENCODES

NAMING — three-letter caps ALWAYS mean a player's real-life NBA team. A fantasy Team is always spelled out plus the acting Manager: 'Lakers — Meakel'. Every BBSL Team is named after an NBA franchise, so without this rule the two collide on the same card, sometimes as the same string.

BOTH GATES — the refusal reports 'Cap · Refused' AND 'Slots · Passed, 10 of 12', every time, neither collapsed.

DISABLED, NOT FAILING — the bid control is disabled with its reason stated, because the next legal bid ($15.0M) is above this Team's Maximum Bid ($14.0M).

ONE SCENARIO THROUGHOUT — $165.0M cap, less $142.0M existing, less $6.0M committed, less $1.0M minors exposure = $16.0M available; less $2.0M reserve = $14.0M maximum bid. It adds up because every BBSL figure sits on the $500k grid.
